title: Method signatures that resist misuse
idea: A misuse-resistant API makes wrong calls fail to compile or fail fast, through precise parameter types, honest return types and no exposed internal state.
points: Distinct types for ids make swapped arguments a compile error, not a data bug.
Replace a boolean flag with an enum so every call site reads clearly.
Return `Optional` for an expected absence; throw when the caller breaks the contract.
Return copies or unmodifiable views; never hand out an internal collection.

hero.title: Reading a signature that resists misuse

parts.label: Honest return
parts.note: A normal refusal can happen. The absence sits in the type, so callers cannot miss it like a null.

parts.label: Verb name
parts.note: Names the caller's intent, not how the method stores anything.

parts.label: Typed id
parts.note: A wrapper record. Passing a Sku here is a compile error, not a corrupted row.

parts.label: Second typed id
parts.note: Two Strings side by side invite swaps. Two distinct types do not.

parts.label: Validated primitive
parts.note: A plain int is fine when the method rejects zero and negatives with a clear message.

parts.label: Enum, not boolean
parts.note: Call sites read REJECT or BACKORDER instead of a bare true.

code.title: The problem
code.caption: Strings, a bare boolean, a null return and a leaked list. Each misuse compiles.

walk.text: Two adjacent `String` parameters and a `boolean`. Nothing at the call site says which is which.
Order and sku are swapped. It compiles, and stock goes negative for a SKU that does not exist.
A negative quantity is accepted and quietly adds stock.
Under the flag, a shortfall returns without a word. The caller cannot tell it failed.
`find` returns `null`, so the crash happens later in the caller, not here.
Returning the internal list lets any caller erase history, as line 18 does.

code.title: The fix
code.caption: Typed ids, an enum policy, `Optional` results and fail-fast checks.

walk.text: `OrderId` and `Sku` wrap strings. Swapping them is now a compile error, as line 12 notes.
The enum replaces `boolean force`. The call site names the policy it chose.
Preconditions fail at once: nulls throw `NullPointerException`, bad values `IllegalArgumentException` with a clear message.
A shortfall under `REJECT` returns `Optional.empty()`. Under `BACKORDER`, stock goes negative on purpose: units owed.
`find` returns `Optional`: a missing order shows in the signature, and callers unwrap it on purpose.
`List.copyOf` hands out an unmodifiable snapshot, never the live list.
Each outcome is visible in the output: success, refusal, backorder, absence and rejection.

pitfalls: Returning `null` from a finder; the NullPointerException appears lines later, far from the cause.
Two adjacent `String` or `int` parameters; a swapped call compiles and corrupts data silently.
Ignoring bad input, like a negative quantity, hides bugs; throw `IllegalArgumentException` instead.

quiz.q: Using the fixed `Inventory`, what does this print?
quiz.why: Stock 2 is short of 3 and the policy is `REJECT`, so `reserve` returns empty before changing stock. Exceptions are only for broken preconditions, like a non-positive quantity.

takeaway: Make wrong calls fail to compile, or fail fast and loudly.

starters: When should a method return Optional instead of throwing an exception?
How many parameters is too many, and what replaces them?
Are wrapper types like Sku worth the extra code in a real codebase?
